question_text: Find the equations of the tangents to the hyperbola 3x² − 4y² = 12 which (i) are parallel to y = x − 7, (ii) are perpendicular to y = x − 7.

insider_note: Both slopes here satisfy |m| = 1 > b/a = √3/2, so a²m² − b² = 1 > 0 and each part gives two genuine tangent lines. Contrast this with a slope where a²m² − b² ≤ 0 — for example an asymptote slope ±b/a — which gives no tangent at all.
formula_note: The tangency condition used here is c² = a²m² − b², with a minus sign, since this is a hyperbola. The matching ellipse condition is c² = a²m² + b², with a plus sign — using it here would give a²m² + b² = 4 + 3 = 7 instead of the 1 actually used, changing every tangent found. Check which conic before writing the sign.

common_mistakes: Using 3 and 4 as a² and b² directly from the given equation, without dividing by 12 first.
Missing that y = x − 7 is already in slope-intercept form, so its slope is simply the coefficient of x.

steps.margin_note: Two marks. a²m² − b² = 1 > 0, so real tangents exist.
steps.memory_tip: Check a²m² − b² before taking the root: here it is 4 − 3 = 1, positive, so two real tangents exist.

steps.why: Real tangents of slope m exist exactly when a²m² − b² > 0. Here a²m² − b² = 4 − 3 = 1 > 0, so the formula gives two genuine parallel tangent lines, one on each side of the hyperbola.
common_mistakes: Writing only one of the two tangent lines instead of both signs of ±1.
Rearranging y = x + 1 incorrectly, e.g. as x + y − 1 = 0 instead of x − y + 1 = 0.
lines_compact: Parallel tangent has the same slope m = 1

steps.label: Perpendicular tangent
steps.memory_tip: The negative reciprocal of 1 is −1 — do not leave it as +1.
